name: skills
readmeExcerpt:
## Android skills

**Android skills** are a dedicated repository of **AI-optimized, modular instructions** and
resources, to help agents better understand and execute specific patterns that follow the best
practices and guidance on Android development
from [developer.android.com](https://developer.android.com).

Android skills follow the [open-standard agent skills](https://agentskills.io/home) - markdown
files (SKILL.md) that provide a technical specification of a task, and **ground LLMs** with
information on specialized domains and workflows.

Our Android skill development focuses on **use cases and workflows where evaluations show LLMs
underperform**.
We aren't prioritizing well-established areas where LLMs are already proficient, such
as basic Jetpack Compose best practices.

To learn more, read the official documentation:

- [Android skills](https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-skills)
- [Android CLI](https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-cli)
- [Android Studio](https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/skills)

### Install Android skills

Use Android CLI to install a specific skill into the current directory:

```
android skills add --skill=r8-analyzer --project=.
```

Use Android CLI to install all Android skills to directories for all detected agents:

```
android skills add --all
```

If you don't have any existing agent directories and don't specify particular agents, the skills
will be installed for Gemini and Antigravity at `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills`.

**Options:**

- `--all` - Add all Android skills. If omitted (and `--skill` isn't specified), only the
  `android-cli` skill will be installed.
- `--agent` - A comma-separated list of agents to install the skill for. If omitted, the skill will
  be installed for all detected agents.
- `--skill` - Specific skill that you want to install. If omitted (and `--all` isn't specified),
  only the `android-cli` skill will be installed.
- `--project` - Path to a project root in which to install the skills.

### Activate skills

Your agent automatically activates skills that are relevant to your task. To use a skill, prompt your agent to complete a task that is related to the skill, for example "Make my app UI edge-to-edge." The agent should automatically find and use the skill if it has been installed.

## Disclaimer

AI can make mistakes, so always double-check the results.

## Contributing

Submit a GitHub issue to provide feedback, report issues, or make new skill requests and changes.

Public contributions are not accepted at this time.

## License

Android Skills is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.txt). See the `LICENSE.txt` file
for
details.

## Review our community guidelines

This project follows
[Google's Open Source Community Guidelines](https://opensource.google/conduct/).

aiSummary.oneLiner: A repository of AI-optimized, modular instructions guiding LLMs to write standard-compliant Android code.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Android Skills provides a dedicated collection of technical specifications formatted as SKILL.md files designed specifically for AI coding assistants. These files act as a crucial grounding mechanism, ensuring AI agents understand and follow the latest best practices and architectural guidance directly from developer.android.com. By feeding these modular instructions into an agent, developers can effectively prevent the AI from hallucinating outdated patterns, such as legacy XML layouts. It forces the language model to generate modern, idiomatic Android development solutions like Jetpack Compose. This open-standard approach targets use cases where LLMs historically underperform, offering a robust way to standardize AI-assisted mobile development.
keyFeatures: Open-standard formatting: Uses the SKILL.md format to provide structured, easily digestible instructions for various AI agents.
Grounding in official docs: Ensures generated code strictly aligns with current recommendations and architectural guidance from developer.android.com.
Modular instruction sets: Allows developers to load specific skills, such as Jetpack Compose or Room, based on the task at hand.
Anti-hallucination mechanism: Actively prevents LLMs from falling back on outdated or deprecated Android development patterns.
AI-optimized writing: The instructions are specifically authored and structured to be easily understood and executed by language models.

useCases.title: Guided AI code generation
useCases.description: Ensures AI coding assistants write modern Android code using current libraries like Jetpack Compose rather than outdated XML layouts.

useCases.title: Standardizing team practices
useCases.description: Provides a shared set of rules that all AI assistants in a team must follow when generating Android components.

useCases.title: Learning modern Android
useCases.description: Helps developers transition to new Android paradigms by forcing the AI assistant to use the correct, modern approach.

useCases.title: Automated refactoring
useCases.description: Assists agents in accurately updating legacy Android code to modern architectural standards.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Android developers and teams using AI coding assistants (like Claude Code or Copilot) who want to enforce modern development standards. It requires a compatible AI agent setup and is ideal for projects heavily relying on AI-assisted coding.
